<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:abelian}
For every $\varphi_F$ the point $\varphi=(\varphi_F,\varphi_D)$ satisfies \eqref{eq:system}
exactly, and its density on the constraint set with respect to $|F|$-dimensional Hausdorff
measure is
\begin{equation}
  \log q_{\mathcal M}(\varphi)=\log q_F(\varphi_F)-\tfrac12\log\det\!\big(\bm I_{|F|}+\bm{\Gamma}^{\!\top}\bm{\Gamma}\big),
  \label{eq:density}
\end{equation}
whose second term is independent of $\varphi_F$ and $b$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The map $\varphi_F\mapsto\varphi$ is the affine embedding $\varphi=\varphi_0(b)+\bm B\varphi_F$
with $\bm B=(\bm I_{|F|},-\bm{\Gamma}^{\!\top})^{\!\top}$, whose volume element
$\sqrt{\det\bm B^{\!\top}\bm B}=\sqrt{\det(\bm I+\bm{\Gamma}^{\!\top}\bm{\Gamma})}$ is a constant.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:torus}
$\varphi_D$ is well defined on $\mathbb{T}^{|D|}$ if and only if $\bm{\Gamma}$ is integer, which holds whenever
$\bm{A}_D$ is unimodular, i.e.\ every elimination pivot is $\pm1$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Under $\varphi_k\mapsto\varphi_k+2\pi$ the solve shifts $\varphi_j$ by $-2\pi\bm{\Gamma}_{jk}$, a multiple
of $2\pi$ if and only if $\bm{\Gamma}_{jk}\in\mathbb{Z}$. All inputs are integer, so a non-integer can arise only
by division, and with every pivot of modulus one no division occurs. (Unimodularity is
sufficient, not necessary: $\bm{A}_D=\bm{A}_F=(2)$ gives $\bm{\Gamma}=(1)$.)
<!-- end proof-2 -->
